How the comparison ran

Three independent Codex iPhone UI reviewers first scored the chosen reference in three task states. Three fresh reviewers rated the reference and all 24 alternatives at 390 pt. Three more reviewed the reference and the highest-scoring option from each family at 440 pt. Ties for that panel went to the shorter populated card, then catalogue order. Opaque IDs and shuffled order kept the reviewers blind to names and previous scores.

Each reviewer scored orientation, scanability, affordance, legibility and composition from zero to two in half-point steps. Each sheet showed the populated task, empty fields and a long hierarchical project with an overdue timed deadline. The two reveal-on-demand layouts also showed their editing face. A score is the mean of three judgments. Compare within a panel, since the width, reviewer and competitors changed.

All layouts use the previous browser prototype, the 12 pt expanded inset, existing multi-edit pickers, checked bottom workspace menu, title-aligned Notes, priority cycle and Adaptive spacing. The two-sided card temporarily dedicates the card to property editing. The drawer adds an intermediate step. Empty-action wording and the overdue tint are shared improvements in the new options. The reference retains its original visual treatment.

Browser checks opened both pickers, changed both values and kept the task expanded in all 150 layout, width and field-state combinations. These are visual studies using standard text in light appearance. Native touch, keyboard behavior, VoiceOver and dark mode were outside the benchmark.
